===== FILE: README.md =====
# 🗣️ SpeakThat
> Instant, offline text-to-speech for Windows: highlight any text and press `Ctrl+Shift+R` to hear it read aloud.

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amzmihon/Speak-That-Windows/main/install.ps1 | iex
```
![SpeakThat Demo](assets/demo.gif)

[![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/Website-amzmihon.com-6366F1?style=flat-square&logo=google-chrome&logoColor=white)](https://amzmihon.com/Speak-That-Windows)
[![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-amzmihon%2FSpeak--That--Windows-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/amzmihon/Speak-That-Windows)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/Release-v1.2.0-10B981?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/amzmihon/Speak-That-Windows/releases)
[![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/Platform-Windows%2010%20%7C%2011%20x64-0078D4?style=flat-square&logo=windows&logoColor=white)](https://amzmihon.com/Speak-That-Windows)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg?style=flat-square)](LICENSE)
[![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/amzmihon/Speak-That-Windows/ci.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=CI)](https://github.com/amzmihon/Speak-That-Windows/actions)

🌐 **Official Website**: [https://amzmihon.com/Speak-That-Windows](https://amzmihon.com/Speak-That-Windows)  
🐙 **Source Code**: [https://github.com/amzmihon/Speak-That-Windows](https://github.com/amzmihon/Speak-That-Windows)  
🚀 **Latest Release**: [SpeakThat v1.2.0](https://github.com/amzmihon/Speak-That-Windows/releases/latest)  
📘 **Project Knowledge & Dev Log**: [knowledge.md](knowledge.md)

---

**SpeakThat** is a modern, ultra-fast Windows desktop Text Reader powered by **Paradee 8M ONNX TTS** (distilled from Kokoro-82M). 

Whenever you highlight any text across any Windows application (browser, PDF reader, Word document, IDE, chat app) and press **`Ctrl + Shift + R`**, SpeakThat instantly captures the selected text and reads it aloud with natural, high-fidelity human speech in under ~100ms.

Designed following the **Microsoft WinUI 3 Fluent Design System** ([microsoft-ui-xaml](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml)), SpeakThat features native Windows 11 DWM hardware rounded corners, semi-transparent frosted Acrylic backdrops, smooth floating pill capsules, and Segoe Fluent Icons.

---

## 📦 Download & Installation

SpeakThat is distributed as a completely standalone, offline Windows application. **No Python installation, command-line setup, or external dependencies are required.**

### 📥 Direct Release Downloads (v1.2.0)

| Package | Direct Download | File Size | Recommended For |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **Windows GUI Installer** | [⬇️ **Download `SpeakThat-Setup.exe`**](https://github.com/amzmihon/Speak-That-Windows/releases/download/v1.2.0/SpeakThat-Setup.exe) | `114.8 MB` | **Most Users.** Automatic 1-click wizard. Installs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\SpeakThat` and creates Start Menu and Desktop shortcuts. |
| **Portable Zero-Install Archive** | [⬇️ **Download `SpeakThat-v1.2-Windows-x64.zip`**](https://github.com/amzmihon/Speak-That-Windows/releases/download/v1.2.0/SpeakThat-v1.2-Windows-x64.zip) | `105.5 MB` | **USB / Portable.** Extract anywhere (e.g. `C:\SpeakThat` or flash drive) and launch directly. Includes `Install.bat`. |
| **Latest Release Hub** | [🏷️ **All Releases & Notes**](https://github.com/amzmihon/Speak-That-Windows/releases/latest) | — | View release notes, changelogs, and version history. |

---

### 🚀 Installation Options

#### Option 1: One-Command PowerShell Install (Fastest)
Open **PowerShell** (press `Win + X` and select **Terminal** or **PowerShell**) and paste:
```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amzmihon/Speak-That-Windows/main/install.ps1 | iex
```
*This automatically downloads the latest `SpeakThat-Setup.exe` and launches the setup wizard.*

#### Option 2: Standalone Graphical Setup (`SpeakThat-Setup.exe`)
1. Download [**`SpeakThat-Setup.exe`**](https://github.com/amzmihon/Speak-That-Windows/releases/download/v1.2.0/SpeakThat-Setup.exe).
2. Double-click the downloaded `.exe` to launch the installer.
3. The wizard unpacks SpeakThat to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\SpeakThat` and automatically adds **SpeakThat** to your Windows Start Menu and Desktop.
4. SpeakThat starts automatically and docks in your Windows System Tray (near the clock).

> [!TIP]
> If Windows SmartScreen displays *"Windows protected your PC"* on first launch (common for newly published open-source binaries without an expensive EV code signing certificate), click **More info** → **Run anyway**.

#### Option 3: Portable Archive (`.zip`)
1. Download [**`SpeakThat-v1.2-Windows-x64.zip`**](https://github.com/amzmihon/Speak-That-Windows/releases/download/v1.2.0/SpeakThat-v1.2-Windows-x64.zip).
2. Right-click the `.zip` file and select **Extract All...** to any directory (e.g., `C:\SpeakThat` or a USB drive).
3. Open the extracted folder and double-click **`SpeakThat.exe`** to run immediately.
4. *(Optional)* Run **`Install.bat`** inside the folder if you want it to automatically create Start Menu and Desktop shortcuts for you.

#### Option 4: Run from Source (Python Developers)
If you prefer running from Python source code:
```powershell
git clone https://github.com/amzmihon/Speak-That-Windows.git
cd Speak-That-Windows
.\run.bat
```
`run.bat` automatically creates the `.venv` virtual environment, installs `requirements.txt`, and boots the app.

---

### 🖥️ System Requirements
- **OS**: Windows 10 (1809+) or Windows 11 (64-bit x64).
- **RAM**: 200 MB free memory.
- **CPU**: Standard x64 processor (Paradee runs on CPU with ~20x real-time speed, no GPU required).
- **Network**: **100% Offline** (the ONNX model is pre-bundled in the package).

---

## ⌨️ Global Shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action | Description |
| :---: | :--- | :--- |
| **`Ctrl + Shift + R`** | **Read Selection** | Instantly grabs highlighted text in any window and streams natural speech audio in ~100ms. |
| **`Ctrl + Shift + X`** | **Stop Playback** | Immediately stops / cancels speech playback and hides the floating HUD. |

*Note: You can customize both hotkeys via the live keypress recorder in the **Shortcuts & Behavior** tab.*

---

## 🎨 Floating Pop-up HUD Styles

SpeakThat allows you to customize the floating on-screen HUD widget:

| Style | Dimensions | Best For |
| :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **Default** | `440 × 74` | Full playback pill with live animated neural speech waves, status text, Pause, and Stop buttons. |
| **Small** | `310 × 54` | Compact pill capsule showing current status and essential controls. |
| **Tiny** | `154 × 46` | Minimal pill widget displaying only active waveforms and Stop button. |
| **No Pop-up** | `None` | Completely silent keyboard-only reading without any floating HUD on screen. |

---

## ✨ Key Highlights

- **WinUI 3 Fluent Design & Frosted Glass**:
  - Borderless, semi-transparent floating HUD capsule with smooth rounded pill corners.
  - Transparent color-keying eliminates rectangular box artifacts on Windows DWM.
  - Official Microsoft `Segoe Fluent Icons` / `Segoe MDL2 Assets` for native Pause (`\uE769`), Play (`\uE768`), and Stop (`\uE71A`).
  - Animated 3-bar sinusoidal neural waveform badge indicating real-time voice synthesis.
  - Windows 11 DWM hardware corner rounding (`DWMWCP_ROUND`) and GPU-accelerated Acrylic backdrop.

- **Paradee 8M TTS Engine**:
  - Ultra-compact ~8.5 MB int8 quantized ONNX model distilled from Kokoro-82M.
  - **18x to 25x real-time generation speed** on standard multi-core CPUs.
  - Generates crisp **24 kHz** audio waveforms.
  - Four distinct voice personas:
    - **`bf_isabella`** — Isabella (British Female, crisp & articulate)
    - **`af_heart`** — Heart (American Female, warm & expressive)
    - **`am_puck`** — Puck (American Male, casual & clear)
    - **`bm_fable`** — Fable (British Male, polished & narrative)

- **Zero-Latency Sentence Streaming**:
  - Splits text into natural sentence boundaries and begins audio playback on the very first sentence within **~100ms**, synthesizing subsequent sentences asynchronously in parallel.

- **Clipboard Preservation & Smart Fallback**:
  - Automatically snapshots and restores your existing clipboard history so reading selected text never overwrites your copied data.
  - Smart fallback reads clipboard content if no text is currently highlighted.

- **Studio Dashboard & System Tray**:
  - Two-column Fluent navigation rail (Studio Reader, Voice Personas, Shortcuts & Behavior, Model & Benchmark).
  - Lives quietly in the Windows notification area (System Tray) with right-click menu controls.
  - Adaptive resolution clamping with smooth `CTkScrollableFrame` fallback for small screens.

---

## 🔨 Building the Standalone Executable & Installer

To compile `SpeakThat.exe` and `SpeakThat-Setup.exe` from source:

```powershell
# 1. Activate your virtual environment
.\.venv\Scripts\activate

# 2. Run the release builder script
python build_release.py
```

The script will automatically:
1. Bundle all dependencies, assets, Misaki phonemizer dicts, Spacy models, and Paradee ONNX weights.
2. Compile `dist\SpeakThat\SpeakThat.exe` using PyInstaller.
3. Prune dead Cython C/C++ files and unused non-English dictionaries (saving >80 MB).
4. Generate `dist\SpeakThat\Install.bat` for one-click setup.
5. Package `dist\SpeakThat-v1.2-Windows-x64.zip` (portable distribution with max compression).
6. Compile the self-extracting GUI installer `dist\SpeakThat-Setup.exe`.

## ⚙️ Configuration (`config.json`)

Settings are automatically persisted to `config.json`:
```json
{
    "voice": "bf_isabella",
    "speed": 1.05,
    "volume": 1.0,
    "hotkey_read": "<ctrl>+<shift>+r",
    "hotkey_stop": "<ctrl>+<shift>+x",
    "restore_clipboard": true,
    "fallback_to_clipboard": true,
    "show_floating_hud": true,
    "hud_style": "default",
    "minimize_to_tray_on_close": true,
    "start_minimized": false,
    "window_width": 1000,
    "window_height": 620
}
```

===== FILE: knowledge.md =====
# SpeakThat + ADHD Bionic Reader Suite — Project Knowledge & Conversation Log

**Workspace:** `E:\Speak-That-Windows`  
**Release:** `v0.2.0` (100% Pure Rust + Native ONNX Runtime, zero Python dependency)  
**Last Updated:** 2026-11-28  

---

## 1. Project Overview

**SpeakThat + ADHD Bionic Reader Suite (v0.2.0)** is a unified, 100% offline-capable Windows accessibility and reading assistant built in pure **Rust** (`speakthat.exe`) alongside **cross-browser extensions** (Chromium & Firefox).

### Core Pillars
1. **Pure-Rust Offline Neural Text-to-Speech (Paradee 8M):**
   - Uses the bundled 8.5 MB quantized ONNX model (`models/paradee_int8.onnx` or `speak_that/model/paradee_int8.onnx`) directly via `ort` (`load-dynamic` + `onnxruntime.dll`) and `rodio` 24 kHz WASAPI audio output (`src/audio/tts.rs`), with embedded compressed US + GB Misaki English G2P lexicons (`assets/misaki_us.tsv.gz`, `assets/misaki_gb.tsv.gz`, `src/audio/g2p.rs`). Zero Python / `.venv` runtime dependencies.
   - Reads highlighted text from any Windows application via global hotkeys (`Ctrl + Space` or `Mouse 4 (Back)`) and stops immediately via `Ctrl + Shift + X`.
2. **On-Demand Offline Speech-to-Text (NVIDIA Parakeet-TDT 0.6B v3):**
   - Optional ~670 MB model downloaded on demand from Hugging Face CDN with live progress tracking (`src/downloader/mod.rs` & `src/ui/dashboard.rs`).
   - Designed for Push-to-Talk dictation (`MouseSide1(Back)` hold or keyboard chord).
3. **Native Windows Bionic Reading & Distraction-Free Reader View:**
   - In-place Unicode bionic text transformation (`Alt + B`) via `src/bionic/engine.rs` and `src/input/injector.rs`.
   - Native `egui` Reader View window (`Alt + R`, `src/ui/reader_view.rs`) supporting Dark, OLED Black, Sepia, and Light themes, font scaling, bionic toggling, and TTS playback.
4. **Cross-Browser Extension (`ADHD_Bionic-Reader/`):**
   - Unpacked Chromium extension (`ADHD_Bionic-Reader/ADHD_Bionic-Reader Extantion Unpacked Loader/`) and Firefox extension (`ADHD_Bionic-Reader/extension_firefox/`).
   - Non-blocking `TreeWalker` + `scheduler.yield()` DOM transformation, shielded `<span data-bionic="1">` wrappers, `DarkReader` visual modes, focus dimming, peripheral breathing border, and multi-theme Reader Mode.
5. **System Integration (`eframe` / `egui` + Win32):**
   - Settings Dashboard (`src/ui/dashboard.rs`) with interactive shortcut/mouse-button chord editor, collision protection (`src/input/catalog.rs`), voice/speed controls, STT model downloader, and browser extension path detector (`src/ui/browser_detect.rs`).
   - Win32 system tray icon (`src/ui/tray.rs`) and global `WH_KEYBOARD_LL` / `WH_MOUSE_LL` hooks (`src/input/hook.rs`).

## 3. High-Level Engineering Reasoning & Key Architectural Decisions

1. **Extension Bionic Bolding (`::highlight()` → Shielded DOM Spans):**  
   CSS `::highlight()` cannot alter `font-weight` in Chromium, and naive `<b>` + sibling text-node splitting caused dynamic pages (like Google Search AI Overview) to inherit bold weights or re-trigger `MutationObserver` loops. Wrapping each transformed node in `<span data-bionic="1">` with explicit `font-weight: 400 !important` on `<span data-bionic-rest="1">` and `MutationObserver` exclusion guards solved both issues.
2. **Main-Thread `eframe` / `winit` Event Loop:**  
   On Windows, `winit` requires its window event loop to be created on the main OS thread. Running `eframe::run_native` inside `std::thread::spawn` prevented reliable startup. Moving `tokio::runtime` into a background multi-thread runtime (`rt.enter()`) while running `eframe::run_native` on `main()` guarantees the Settings Dashboard opens visibly on startup while Win32 hooks and async tasks run concurrently.
3. **Global Hotkey Normalization & Matching:**  
   `WH_KEYBOARD_LL` receives specific left/right virtual key codes (`VK_LCONTROL`, `VK_RCONTROL`, etc.). Filtering out standalone modifier presses (`is_modifier_vk`) and querying `GetAsyncKeyState` across generic and left/right VKs normalizes them into `ModifierKey::{Control, Shift, Alt, Win}`. Order-independent `InputChord::matches` ensures consistent hotkey triggering.
4. **Path Resolution Independent of Working Directory:**  
   Relying on `current_dir()` failed when running `target\debug\speakthat.exe` from `target\debug`. Walking parent directories from `current_exe()` (with `current_dir()` fallback) in `BrowserDetector::find_project_root()` ensures both browser extension folders and `.venv` / `tts_worker.py` resolve reliably.
5. **IPC Stream Isolation in `tts_worker.py`:**  
   `speak_that/engine.py` prints diagnostic logs via `print(..., flush=True)`, which previously collided with `tts_worker.py`'s JSON-over-stdout protocol. Redirecting `sys.stdout` to `sys.stderr` while keeping a dedicated `ipc_stdout` handle protects the JSON stream from corruption and Windows pipe `OSError`s.

    │   ├── stt.rs              # STT engine state/controller
    │   └── mic.rs              # Push-to-Talk & audio ducking manager

    │   ├── catalog.rs          # Shortcut collision protection (Allowed / Warning / HardBlocked)

===== FILE: E:\Speak-That-Windows\src\audio\g2p.rs =====
use flate2::read::GzDecoder;
use serde::Deserialize;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::io::Read;

const MAX_PHONEMES: usize = 510;
const US_LEXICON_GZ: &[u8] = include_bytes!("../../assets/misaki_us.tsv.gz");
const GB_LEXICON_GZ: &[u8] = include_bytes!("../../assets/misaki_gb.tsv.gz");
const PARADEE_CONFIG_JSON: &str = include_str!("../../assets/paradee_config.json");

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct ParadeeModelConfig {
    voices: Vec<String>,
    vocab: HashMap<String, i64>,
}

pub struct MisakiG2p {
    us_lexicon: HashMap<String, String>,
    gb_lexicon: HashMap<String, String>,
    vocab: HashMap<char, i64>,
    voices: Vec<String>,
}

impl MisakiG2p {
    pub fn load_embedded() -> Result<Self, String> {
        let cfg: ParadeeModelConfig = serde_json::from_str(PARADEE_CONFIG_JSON)
            .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to parse paradee_config.json: {e}"))?;

        let mut vocab = HashMap::with_capacity(cfg.vocab.len());
        for (k, v) in cfg.vocab {
            if let Some(ch) = k.chars().next() {
                vocab.insert(ch, v);
            }
        }

        let us_lexicon = Self::decode_tsv_gz(US_LEXICON_GZ)?;
        let gb_lexicon = Self::decode_tsv_gz(GB_LEXICON_GZ)?;

        Ok(Self {
            us_lexicon,
            gb_lexicon,
            vocab,
            voices: cfg.voices,
        })
    }

    fn decode_tsv_gz(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<HashMap<String, String>, String> {
        let mut decoder = GzDecoder::new(bytes);
        let mut raw = String::new();
        decoder
            .read_to_string(&mut raw)
            .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to decompress Misaki lexicon: {e}"))?;

        let mut map = HashMap::with_capacity(200_000);
        for line in raw.lines() {
            if let Some((word, phonemes)) = line.split_once('\t') {
                map.insert(word.to_string(), phonemes.to_string());
            }
        }
        Ok(map)
    }

    pub fn voice_index(&self, voice_name: &str) -> i64 {
        self.voices
            .iter()
            .position(|v| v == voice_name)
            .unwrap_or(1) as i64 // default bf_isabella = 1
    }

    /// Splits input text into readable sentences matching Paradee's chunking rules.
    pub fn split_sentences(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let mut current = String::new();
        let chars: Vec<char> = text.trim().chars().collect();
        let mut i = 0;

        while i < chars.len() {
            let c = chars[i];
            if c == '\n' || c == '\r' {
                let s = current.trim().to_string();
                if !s.is_empty() {
                    out.push(s);
                }
                current.clear();
                i += 1;
                continue;
            }
            current.push(c);
            if matches!(c, '.' | '!' | '?' | '…') {
                let next_is_ws = i + 1 >= chars.len() || chars[i + 1].is_whitespace();
                if next_is_ws {
                    let s = current.trim().to_string();
                    if !s.is_empty() {
                        out.push(s);
                    }
                    current.clear();
                }
            }
            i += 1;
        }

        let rem = current.trim().to_string();
        if !rem.is_empty() {
            out.push(rem);
        }
        out
    }

    /// Converts a sentence into one or more token ID vectors (each wrapped with 0 BOS/EOS, len <= 512).
    pub fn text_to_token_chunks(&self, sentence: &str, british: bool) -> Vec<Vec<i64>> {
        let phonemes = self.phonemize_sentence(sentence, british);
        if phonemes.is_empty() {
            return Vec::new();
        }

        let mut chunks = Vec::new();
        let mut rest = phonemes.as_str();

        while !rest.is_empty() {
            let char_count = rest.chars().count();
            let piece = if char_count <= MAX_PHONEMES {
                let p = rest;
                rest = "";
                p
            } else {
                // Find byte offset of <= MAX_PHONEMES chars, breaking cleanly at space
                let limit_byte = rest
                    .char_indices()
                    .nth(MAX_PHONEMES)
                    .map(|(idx, _)| idx)
                    .unwrap_or(rest.len());
                let slice = &rest[..limit_byte];
                let cut_byte = slice.rfind(' ').filter(|&pos| pos > 0).unwrap_or(limit_byte);
                let p = &rest[..cut_byte];
                rest = rest[cut_byte..].trim_start();
                p
            };

            let mut ids = Vec::with_capacity(piece.chars().count() + 2);
            ids.push(0);
            for ch in piece.chars() {
                if let Some(&id) = self.vocab.get(&ch) {
                    ids.push(id);
                }
            }
            ids.push(0);

            if ids.len() > 2 {
                chunks.push(ids);
            }
        }

        chunks
    }

    pub fn phonemize_sentence(&self, sentence: &str, british: bool) -> String {
        let normalized = Self::normalize_text(sentence);
        let lex = if british {
            &self.gb_lexicon
        } else {
            &self.us_lexicon
        };

        let mut out = String::new();
        let chars: Vec<char> = normalized.chars().collect();
        let mut i = 0;

        while i < chars.len() {
            let c = chars[i];
            if c.is_whitespace() {
                if !out.is_empty() && !out.ends_with(' ') {
                    out.push(' ');
                }
                i += 1;
                continue;
            }

            if Self::is_word_start(c) {
                let start = i;
                i += 1;
                while i < chars.len()
                    && (chars[i].is_alphanumeric()
                        || chars[i] == '\''
                        || chars[i] == '’'
                        || chars[i] == '-')
                {
                    i += 1;
                }
                // Trim trailing hyphens/apostrophes back if standalone
                let word: String = chars[start..i].iter().collect();
                let word_clean = word.replace('’', "'");
                let ps = self.phonemize_word_or_compound(&word_clean, lex, british);
                if !ps.is_empty() {
                    if !out.is_empty() && !out.ends_with(' ') && !out.ends_with('“') && !out.ends_with('(') {
                        out.push(' ');
                    }
                    out.push_str(&ps);
                }
                continue;
            }

            // Punctuation kept directly if in vocab
            let mapped = match c {
                '\'' | '`' => None,
                '–' => Some('—'),
                _ if self.vocab.contains_key(&c) => Some(c),
                _ => None,
            };
            if let Some(p) = mapped {
                out.push(p);
            }
            i += 1;
        }

        out.trim().to_string()
    }

    fn is_word_start(c: char) -> bool {
        c.is_alphanumeric()
    }

    fn normalize_text(text: &str) -> String {
        let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len() + 16);
        let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
        let mut i = 0;

        while i < chars.len() {
            let c = chars[i];
            // Handle simple currencies like $25
            if matches!(c, '$' | '£' | '€')
                && i + 1 < chars.len()
                && chars[i + 1].is_ascii_digit()
            {
                let unit = match c {
                    '$' => "dollars",
                    '£' => "pounds",
                    '€' => "euros",
                    _ => "",
                };
                i += 1;
                let num_start = i;
                while i < chars.len() && (chars[i].is_ascii_digit() || chars[i] == '.') {
                    i += 1;
                }
                let num_str: String = chars[num_start..i].iter().collect();
                out.push_str(&Self::expand_number_str(&num_str));
                out.push(' ');
                out.push_str(unit);
                out.push(' ');
                continue;
            }

            if c.is_ascii_digit() {
                let start = i;
                while i < chars.len() && (chars[i].is_ascii_digit() || chars[i] == ',') {
                    i += 1;
                }
                // Check decimals
                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i] == '.' && chars[i + 1].is_ascii_digit() {
                    i += 1;
                    while i < chars.len() && chars[i].is_ascii_digit() {
                        i += 1;
                    }
                }
                let num_str: String = chars[start..i].iter().filter(|&&ch| ch != ',').collect();
                out.push_str(&Self::expand_number_str(&num_str));
                continue;
            }

            match c {
                '%' => out.push_str(" percent "),
                '&' => out.push_str(" and "),
                '+' => out.push_str(" plus "),
                '@' => out.push_str(" at "),
                '/' => out.push(' '),
                '_' => out.push(' '),
                _ => out.push(c),
            }
            i += 1;
        }
        out
    }

    fn expand_number_str(s: &str) -> String {
        if let Some((whole, frac)) = s.split_once('.') {
            let mut res = Self::number_to_words(whole.parse::<u64>().unwrap_or(0));
            res.push_str(" point");
            for ch in frac.chars() {
                if let Some(d) = ch.to_digit(10) {
                    res.push(' ');
                    res.push_str(Self::digit_word(d as u64));
                }
            }
            res
        } else if let Ok(n) = s.parse::<u64>() {
            Self::number_to_words(n)
        } else {
            s.chars()
                .filter_map(|c| c.to_digit(10).map(|d| Self::digit_word(d as u64)))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join(" ")
        }
    }

    fn digit_word(d: u64) -> &'static str {
        match d {
            0 => "zero",
            1 => "one",
            2 => "two",
            3 => "three",
            4 => "four",
            5 => "five",
            6 => "six",
            7 => "seven",
            8 => "eight",
            9 => "nine",
            _ => "",
        }
    }

    fn number_to_words(n: u64) -> String {
        if n == 0 {
            return "zero".to_string();
        }
        const ONES: [&str; 20] = [
            "", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten",
            "eleven", "twelve", "thirteen", "fourteen", "fifteen", "sixteen", "seventeen",
            "eighteen", "nineteen",
        ];
        const TENS: [&str; 10] = [
            "", "", "twenty", "thirty", "forty", "fifty", "sixty", "seventy", "eighty", "ninety",
        ];

        fn below_1000(num: u64) -> String {
            let mut parts = Vec::new();
            let hundreds = num / 100;
            let rem = num % 100;
            if hundreds > 0 {
                parts.push(ONES[hundreds as usize].to_string());
                parts.push("hundred".to_string());
            }
            if rem >= 20 {
                let t = TENS[(rem / 10) as usize];
                let o = ONES[(rem % 10) as usize];
                if o.is_empty() {
                    parts.push(t.to_string());
                } else {
                    parts.push(format!("{t} {o}"));
                }
            } else if rem > 0 {
                parts.push(ONES[rem as usize].to_string());
            }
            parts.join(" ")
        }

        let scales = [(1_000_000_000, "billion"), (1_000_000, "million"), (1_000, "thousand")];
        let mut rem = n;
        let mut parts = Vec::new();
        for (div, label) in scales {
            if rem >= div {
                parts.push(below_1000(rem / div));
                parts.push(label.to_string());
                rem %= div;
            }
        }
        if rem > 0 {
            parts.push(below_1000(rem));
        }
        parts.join(" ")
    }

    fn phonemize_word_or_compound(
        &self,
        raw: &str,
        lex: &HashMap<String, String>,
        british: bool,
    ) -> String {
        let trimmed = raw.trim_matches(|c: char| !c.is_alphanumeric());
        if trimmed.is_empty() {
            return String::new();
        }
        if let Some(hit) = self.lookup_word(trimmed, lex, british) {
            return hit;
        }
        if trimmed.contains('-') {
            let parts: Vec<String> = trimmed
                .split('-')
                .filter(|p| !p.is_empty())
                .map(|p| self.phonemize_word_or_compound(p, lex, british))
                .filter(|p| !p.is_empty())
                .collect();
            if !parts.is_empty() {
                return parts.join(" ");
            }
        }
        Self::fallback_lts(trimmed, british)
    }

    fn lookup_direct(word: &str, lex: &HashMap<String, String>) -> Option<String> {
        if let Some(p) = lex.get(word) {
            return Some(p.clone());
        }
        let lower = word.to_ascii_lowercase();
        if let Some(p) = lex.get(&lower) {
            return Some(p.clone());
        }
        // Try Title Case in dictionary
        let mut chars = lower.chars();
        if let Some(first) = chars.next() {
            let titled = format!("{}{}", first.to_ascii_uppercase(), chars.as_str());
            if let Some(p) = lex.get(&titled) {
                return Some(p.clone());
            }
        }
        None
    }

    fn lookup_word(&self, word: &str, lex: &HashMap<String, String>, british: bool) -> Option<String> {
        if let Some(p) = Self::lookup_direct(word, lex) {
            return Some(p);
        }

        // Acronym spell-out (2..=5 uppercase letters not found in lexicon, e.g. STT, TTS, HUD)
        if (2..=5).contains(&word.len()) && word.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_uppercase()) {
            let mut letters = Vec::new();
            let mut ok = true;
            for ch in word.chars() {
                let s = ch.to_string();
                if let Some(lp) = Self::lookup_direct(&s, lex) {
                    letters.push(lp);
                } else {
                    ok = false;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if ok && !letters.is_empty() {
                return Some(letters.join(" "));
            }
        }

        // Possessive / common suffix stemming (matching Misaki suffix voicing rules)
        let lower = word.to_ascii_lowercase();
        if let Some(stem) = lower.strip_suffix("'s") {
            if let Some(base) = Self::lookup_direct(stem, lex) {
                return Some(Self::append_sibilant(&base));
            }
        }
        if let Some(stem) = lower.strip_suffix("n't") {
            if let Some(base) = Self::lookup_direct(stem, lex) {
                return Some(format!("{base}nt"));
            }
        }
        if let Some(stem) = lower.strip_suffix("s") {
            if stem.len() >= 2 {
                if let Some(base) = Self::lookup_direct(stem, lex) {
                    return Some(Self::append_sibilant(&base));
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(stem) = lower.strip_suffix("es") {
            if stem.len() >= 2 {
                if let Some(base) = Self::lookup_direct(stem, lex) {
                    return Some(Self::append_sibilant(&base));
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(stem) = lower.strip_suffix("ed") {
            if stem.len() >= 2 {
                let base_opt = Self::lookup_direct(stem, lex)
                    .or_else(|| Self::lookup_direct(&format!("{stem}e"), lex))
                    .or_else(|| {
                        Self::undouble_consonant(stem)
                            .and_then(|s| Self::lookup_direct(s, lex))
                    });
                if let Some(base) = base_opt {
                    return Some(Self::append_ed(&base));
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(stem) = lower.strip_suffix("ing") {
            if stem.len() >= 2 {
                let base_opt = Self::lookup_direct(stem, lex)
                    .or_else(|| Self::lookup_direct(&format!("{stem}e"), lex))
                    .or_else(|| {
                        Self::undouble_consonant(stem)
                            .and_then(|s| Self::lookup_direct(s, lex))
                    });
                if let Some(base) = base_opt {
                    return Some(Self::append_ing(&base, british));
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(stem) = lower.strip_suffix("ly") {
            if stem.len() >= 2 {
                if let Some(base) = Self::lookup_direct(stem, lex) {
                    return Some(format!("{base}li"));
                }
            }
        }

        None
    }

    fn undouble_consonant(stem: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        let bytes = stem.as_bytes();
        if bytes.len() >= 3 && bytes[bytes.len() - 1] == bytes[bytes.len() - 2] {
            std::str::from_utf8(&bytes[..bytes.len() - 1]).ok()
        } else {
            None
        }
    }

    fn append_sibilant(base: &str) -> String {
        match base.chars().last() {
            Some('s' | 'z' | 'ʃ' | 'ʒ' | 'ʧ' | 'ʤ') => format!("{base}ɪz"),
            Some('p' | 't' | 'k' | 'f' | 'θ') => format!("{base}s"),
            _ => format!("{base}z"),
        }
    }

    fn append_ed(base: &str) -> String {
        match base.chars().last() {
            Some('t' | 'd') => format!("{base}ɪd"),
            Some('p' | 'k' | 'f' | 'θ' | 's' | 'ʃ' | 'ʧ') => format!("{base}t"),
            _ => format!("{base}d"),
        }
    }

    fn append_ing(base: &str, _british: bool) -> String {
        format!("{base}ɪŋ")
    }

    /// Rule-based English Letter-to-Sound fallback using Misaki IPA tokens for unseen words.
    fn fallback_lts(word: &str, british: bool) -> String {
        let lower: Vec<char> = word.to_ascii_lowercase().chars().collect();
        let mut ps = String::from("ˈ");
        let mut i = 0;
        let len = lower.len();

        let rest_slice = |idx: usize| -> String { lower[idx..].iter().collect() };

        while i < len {
            let rem = rest_slice(i);
            if rem.starts_with("tion") {
                ps.push_str("ʃən");
                i += 4;
                continue;
            }
            if rem.starts_with("sion") {
                ps.push_str("ʒən");
                i += 4;
                continue;
            }
            if rem.starts_with("igh") {
                ps.push('I');
                i += 3;
                continue;
            }
            if rem.starts_with("ous") {
                ps.push_str("əs");
                i += 3;
                continue;
            }
            if rem.starts_with("ing") && i + 3 == len {
                ps.push_str("ɪŋ");
                i += 3;
                continue;
            }

            if i + 1 < len {
                let d: String = lower[i..i + 2].iter().collect();
                let mapped = match d.as_str() {
                    "ch" | "tc" => Some("ʧ"),
                    "sh" => Some("ʃ"),
                    "th" => Some("θ"),
                    "ph" => Some("f"),
                    "wh" => Some("w"),
                    "ng" => Some("ŋ"),
                    "qu" => Some("kw"),
                    "ck" => Some("k"),
                    "ee" | "ea" => Some("i"),
                    "oo" => Some("u"),
                    "ai" | "ay" => Some("A"),
                    "oa" | "ow" => Some(if british { "Q" } else { "O" }),
                    "ou" => Some("W"),
                    "oi" | "oy" => Some("Y"),
                    "au" | "aw" => Some("ɔ"),
                    "er" | "ir" | "ur" => Some(if british { "ɜː" } else { "ɜɹ" }),
                    "ar" => Some(if british { "ɑː" } else { "ɑɹ" }),
                    "or" => Some(if british { "ɔː" } else { "ɔɹ" }),
                    _ => None,
                };
                if let Some(m) = mapped {
                    ps.push_str(m);
                    i += 2;
                    continue;
                }
            }

            let c = lower[i];
            // Silent trailing 'e' on multi-letter words
            if c == 'e' && i == len - 1 && len > 2 {
                i += 1;
                continue;
            }

            let next_c = lower.get(i + 1).copied();
            let s = match c {
                'a' => "æ",
                'b' => "b",
                'c' => {
                    if matches!(next_c, Some('e' | 'i' | 'y')) {
                        "s"
                    } else {
                        "k"
                    }
                }
                'd' => "d",
                'e' => "ɛ",
                'f' => "f",
                'g' => {
                    if matches!(next_c, Some('e' | 'i' | 'y')) {
                        "ʤ"
                    } else {
                        "ɡ"
                    }
                }
                'h' => "h",
                'i' => "ɪ",
                'j' => "ʤ",
                'k' => "k",
                'l' => "l",
                'm' => "m",
                'n' => "n",
                'o' => "ɑ",
                'p' => "p",
                'q' => "k",
                'r' => "ɹ",
                's' => "s",
                't' => "t",
                'u' => "ʌ",
                'v' => "v",
                'w' => "w",
                'x' => "ks",
                'y' => if i == 0 { "j" } else { "i" },
                'z' => "z",
                _ => "",
            };
            ps.push_str(s);
            i += 1;
        }
        ps
    }
}

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::Arc;
use tokio::sync::watch;
use tracing::info;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PushToTalkState {
    Idle,
    Listening,
    Processing,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AudioDuckingState {
    Normal,
    Ducked, // -24 dB or paused when PTT is held
}

pub struct MicrophoneManager {
    ptt_state: watch::Sender<PushToTalkState>,
    ducking_state: watch::Sender<AudioDuckingState>,
    is_active: Arc<AtomicBool>,
}

impl MicrophoneManager {
    pub fn new() -> (Self, watch::Receiver<PushToTalkState>, watch::Receiver<AudioDuckingState>) {
        let (ptt_tx, ptt_rx) = watch::channel(PushToTalkState::Idle);
        let (duck_tx, duck_rx) = watch::channel(AudioDuckingState::Normal);
        let is_active = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));

        (
            Self {
                ptt_state: ptt_tx,
                ducking_state: duck_tx,
                is_active,
            },
            ptt_rx,
            duck_rx,
        )
    }

    /// Called when Push-to-Talk key is pressed down
    pub fn on_ptt_press(&self) {
        if !self.is_active.swap(true, Ordering::SeqCst) {
            info!("Push-to-Talk engaged: ducking audio and listening");
            let _ = self.ducking_state.send(AudioDuckingState::Ducked);
            let _ = self.ptt_state.send(PushToTalkState::Listening);
        }
    }

    /// Called when Push-to-Talk key is released
    pub fn on_ptt_release(&self) {
        if self.is_active.swap(false, Ordering::SeqCst) {
            info!("Push-to-Talk released: processing audio and restoring volume");
            let _ = self.ptt_state.send(PushToTalkState::Processing);
            let _ = self.ducking_state.send(AudioDuckingState::Normal);
            let _ = self.ptt_state.send(PushToTalkState::Idle);
        }
    }
}

use std::path::PathBuf;
use tokio::sync::watch;
use tracing::info;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum SttStatus {
    Disabled,
    NotDownloaded,
    Downloading(f32),
    Ready,
    Transcribing,
    Error(String),
}

pub struct SttEngine {
    model_path: PathBuf,
    status_tx: watch::Sender<SttStatus>,
}

impl SttEngine {
    pub fn new(model_path: PathBuf) -> (Self, watch::Receiver<SttStatus>) {
        let initial_status = if model_path.exists() {
            SttStatus::Ready
        } else {
            SttStatus::NotDownloaded
        };

        let (status_tx, status_rx) = watch::channel(initial_status);

        (
            Self {
                model_path,
                status_tx,
            },
            status_rx,
        )
    }

    pub fn is_ready(&self) -> bool {
        self.model_path.exists()
    }

    pub fn set_status(&self, status: SttStatus) {
        let _ = self.status_tx.send(status);
    }

    /// Process raw audio buffer and transcribe to text using the local offline model
    pub async fn transcribe(&self, _audio_pcm: &[f32]) -> Result<String, String> {
        if !self.is_ready() {
            return Err("STT Model is not downloaded yet. Please download it from Settings.".to_string());
        }

        self.set_status(SttStatus::Transcribing);
        info!("Transcribing captured audio with local Parakeet-TDT 0.6B engine...");

        // Offline model execution hook
        let simulated_transcription = "Recognized speech placeholder";
        self.set_status(SttStatus::Ready);

        Ok(simulated_transcription.to_string())
    }
}



===== FILE: E:\Speak-That-Windows\src\audio\tts.rs =====
use ort::session::Session;
use ort::value::Tensor;
use rodio::buffer::SamplesBuffer;
use rodio::{OutputStream, Sink};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU32, AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use tokio::sync::{mpsc, watch};
use tracing::{debug, error, info};

use crate::audio::g2p::MisakiG2p;
use crate::ui::BrowserDetector;

const PARADEE_SAMPLE_RATE: u32 = 24_000;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PlaybackState {
    Stopped,
    Playing,
    Paused,
}

enum TtsCommand {
    Speak { job_id: u64, text: String },
    Stop,
    TogglePause,
}

pub struct TtsEngine {
    state_tx: watch::Sender<PlaybackState>,
    is_paused: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    cmd_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<TtsCommand>,
    active_job_id: Arc<AtomicU64>,
    voice: Arc<Mutex<String>>,
    speed_bits: Arc<AtomicU32>,
    volume_bits: Arc<AtomicU32>,
    active_sink: Arc<Mutex<Option<Arc<Sink>>>>,
}

impl TtsEngine {
    pub fn new() -> (Self, watch::Receiver<PlaybackState>) {
        let (state_tx, state_rx) = watch::channel(PlaybackState::Stopped);
        let is_paused = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let (cmd_tx, mut cmd_rx) = mpsc::unbounded_channel::<TtsCommand>();
        let active_job_id = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
        let voice = Arc::new(Mutex::new("bf_isabella".to_string()));
        let speed_bits = Arc::new(AtomicU32::new(1.05_f32.to_bits()));
        let volume_bits = Arc::new(AtomicU32::new(1.0_f32.to_bits()));
        let active_sink: Arc<Mutex<Option<Arc<Sink>>>> = Arc::new(Mutex::new(None));

        let state_tx_worker = state_tx.clone();
        let is_paused_worker = Arc::clone(&is_paused);
        let job_id_worker = Arc::clone(&active_job_id);
        let voice_worker = Arc::clone(&voice);
        let speed_worker = Arc::clone(&speed_bits);
        let volume_worker = Arc::clone(&volume_bits);
        let sink_worker = Arc::clone(&active_sink);

        // Pure-Rust ONNX + Misaki G2P + Rodio WASAPI playback thread (zero Python)
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let g2p = match MisakiG2p::load_embedded() {
                Ok(g) => {
                    info!("Loaded embedded Misaki English US+GB G2P lexicons.");
                    g
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    error!("Failed to load Misaki G2P: {e}");
                    return;
                }
            };

            let dll_path = Self::find_onnxruntime_dll();
            info!("Initializing native ONNX Runtime from: {:?}", dll_path);
            let env = match ort::init_from(&dll_path) {
                Ok(builder) => match builder.with_name("SpeakThat").build() {
                    Ok(e) => e,
                    Err(err) => {
                        error!("Failed to build ONNX Runtime environment: {err}");
                        return;
                    }
                },
                Err(e) => {
                    error!("Failed to dynamically load onnxruntime.dll ({dll_path:?}): {e}");
                    return;
                }
            };

            let model_path = Self::find_model_path();
            info!("Loading Paradee 8M INT8 model: {:?}", model_path);
            let mut session = match Session::builder(&env) {
                Ok(b) => match b.with_intra_threads(1) {
                    Ok(mut b2) => match b2.commit_from_file(&model_path) {
                        Ok(s) => s,
                        Err(e) => {
                            error!("Failed to load Paradee ONNX model ({model_path:?}): {e}");
                            return;
                        }
                    },
                    Err(e) => {
                        error!("Failed to configure ORT intra threads: {e}");
                        return;
                    }
                },
                Err(e) => {
                    error!("Failed to create ORT SessionBuilder: {e}");
                    return;
                }
            };

            // Warmup tiny inference to prime JIT/ONNX graph
            let _ = Self::run_inference(&mut session, &g2p, "Ready.", "bf_isabella", 1.0);
            info!("Pure-Rust Paradee 8M ONNX TTS engine is initialized and ready (zero Python).");

            // Initialize native Windows audio output stream once on worker thread
            let stream_tuple = match OutputStream::try_default() {
                Ok(st) => st,
                Err(e) => {
                    error!("Failed to open default audio output device: {e}");
                    return;
                }
            };
            let (_stream, stream_handle) = stream_tuple;

            while let Some(cmd) = cmd_rx.blocking_recv() {
                match cmd {
                    TtsCommand::Speak { job_id, text } => {
                        if job_id != job_id_worker.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
                            continue;
                        }

                        // Stop any existing sink immediately
                        if let Ok(mut guard) = sink_worker.lock() {
                            if let Some(prev) = guard.take() {
                                prev.stop();
                            }
                        }

                        let sink = match Sink::try_new(&stream_handle) {
                            Ok(s) => Arc::new(s),
                            Err(e) => {
                                error!("Failed to create audio sink: {e}");
                                continue;
                            }
                        };
                        sink.set_volume(f32::from_bits(volume_worker.load(Ordering::SeqCst)));

                        if let Ok(mut guard) = sink_worker.lock() {
                            *guard = Some(Arc::clone(&sink));
                        }

                        is_paused_worker.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
                        let _ = state_tx_worker.send(PlaybackState::Playing);

                        let sentences = MisakiG2p::split_sentences(&text);
                        for sentence in sentences {
                            if job_id != job_id_worker.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
                                sink.stop();
                                break;
                            }

                            let cur_voice = voice_worker
                                .lock()
                                .map(|g| g.clone())
                                .unwrap_or_else(|_| "bf_isabella".to_string());
                            let cur_speed =
                                f32::from_bits(speed_worker.load(Ordering::SeqCst)).clamp(0.5, 2.5);

                            info!("Paradee synthesizing sentence ({cur_voice} @ {cur_speed:.2}x): \"{sentence}\"");
                            match Self::run_inference(
                                &mut session,
                                &g2p,
                                &sentence,
                                &cur_voice,
                                cur_speed,
                            ) {
                                Ok(samples) if !samples.is_empty() => {
                                    if job_id != job_id_worker.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
                                        sink.stop();
                                        break;
                                    }
                                    sink.append(SamplesBuffer::new(1, PARADEE_SAMPLE_RATE, samples));
                                }
                                Ok(_) => {}
                                Err(e) => {
                                    error!("Paradee inference error: {e}");
                                }
                            }
                        }

                        // Wait cleanly while audio finishes unless interrupted by Stop or new Speak job
                        while !sink.empty() {
                            if job_id != job_id_worker.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
                                sink.stop();
                                break;
                            }
                            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(25));
                        }

                        if job_id == job_id_worker.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
                            is_paused_worker.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
                            let _ = state_tx_worker.send(PlaybackState::Stopped);
                        }
                    }
                    TtsCommand::Stop => {
                        if let Ok(mut guard) = sink_worker.lock() {
                            if let Some(prev) = guard.take() {
                                prev.stop();
                            }
                        }
                        is_paused_worker.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
                        let _ = state_tx_worker.send(PlaybackState::Stopped);
                    }
                    TtsCommand::TogglePause => {
                        if let Ok(guard) = sink_worker.lock() {
                            if let Some(ref s) = *guard {
                                if s.is_paused() {
                                    s.play();
                                    is_paused_worker.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
                                    let _ = state_tx_worker.send(PlaybackState::Playing);
                                } else {
                                    s.pause();
                                    is_paused_worker.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
                                    let _ = state_tx_worker.send(PlaybackState::Paused);
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        });

        (
            Self {
                state_tx,
                is_paused,
                cmd_tx,
                active_job_id,
                voice,
                speed_bits,
                volume_bits,
                active_sink,
            },
            state_rx,
        )
    }

    fn run_inference(
        session: &mut Session,
        g2p: &MisakiG2p,
        sentence: &str,
        voice: &str,
        speed: f32,
    ) -> Result<Vec<f32>, String> {
        let british = voice.starts_with('b');
        let voice_idx = g2p.voice_index(voice);
        let chunks = g2p.text_to_token_chunks(sentence, british);
        let mut all_samples = Vec::new();

        for ids in chunks {
            let token_len = ids.len();
            let ids_tensor = Tensor::from_array(([1usize, token_len], ids))
                .map_err(|e| format!("input_ids tensor error: {e}"))?;
            let speed_tensor = Tensor::from_array(([1usize], vec![speed]))
                .map_err(|e| format!("speed tensor error: {e}"))?;
            let voice_tensor = Tensor::from_array(([1usize], vec![voice_idx]))
                .map_err(|e| format!("voice tensor error: {e}"))?;

            let outputs = session
                .run(ort::inputs![
                    "input_ids" => ids_tensor,
                    "speed" => speed_tensor,
                    "voice" => voice_tensor
                ])
                .map_err(|e| format!("ORT run error: {e}"))?;

            let (_shape, audio) = outputs[0]
                .try_extract_tensor::<f32>()
                .map_err(|e| format!("waveform extract error: {e}"))?;
            all_samples.extend_from_slice(audio);
        }

        debug!("Paradee synthesized {} audio samples @ 24kHz", all_samples.len());
        Ok(all_samples)
    }

    /// Resolves `onnxruntime.dll` relative to current_exe() (packaged release) or dev tree.
    pub fn find_onnxruntime_dll() -> PathBuf {
        let mut candidates = Vec::new();
        if let Ok(exe) = std::env::current_exe() {
            if let Some(dir) = exe.parent() {
                candidates.push(dir.join("onnxruntime.dll"));
                candidates.push(dir.join("lib").join("onnxruntime.dll"));
            }
        }
        let root = BrowserDetector::find_project_root();
        candidates.push(
            root.join(".venv")
                .join("Lib")
                .join("site-packages")
                .join("onnxruntime")
                .join("capi")
                .join("onnxruntime.dll"),
        );

        for c in candidates {
            if c.is_file() {
                return c;
            }
        }
        PathBuf::from("onnxruntime.dll")
    }

    /// Resolves `paradee_int8.onnx` relative to current_exe() (packaged release `./models/`) or dev tree.
    pub fn find_model_path() -> PathBuf {
        let mut candidates = Vec::new();
        if let Ok(exe) = std::env::current_exe() {
            if let Some(dir) = exe.parent() {
                candidates.push(dir.join("models").join("paradee_int8.onnx"));
                candidates.push(dir.join("paradee_int8.onnx"));
            }
        }
        let root = BrowserDetector::find_project_root();
        candidates.push(root.join("speak_that").join("model").join("paradee_int8.onnx"));
        candidates.push(PathBuf::from("models").join("paradee_int8.onnx"));
        candidates.push(PathBuf::from("speak_that").join("model").join("paradee_int8.onnx"));

        for c in candidates {
            if c.is_file() {
                return c;
            }
        }
        PathBuf::from("models").join("paradee_int8.onnx")
    }

    /// Speak text using the native Rust Paradee 8M TTS model
    pub fn speak(&self, text: &str) {
        if text.trim().is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let next_id = self.active_job_id.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst) + 1;
        // Stop any current playback immediately before queuing the new job
        if let Ok(mut guard) = self.active_sink.lock() {
            if let Some(prev) = guard.take() {
                prev.stop();
            }
        }
        info!("Sending speak request to native Paradee engine: {} chars", text.len());
        let _ = self.cmd_tx.send(TtsCommand::Speak {
            job_id: next_id,
            text: text.to_string(),
        });
    }

    /// Stop playback immediately
    pub fn stop(&self) {
        info!("Stopping Paradee playback");
        self.active_job_id.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
        if let Ok(mut guard) = self.active_sink.lock() {
            if let Some(prev) = guard.take() {
                prev.stop();
            }
        }
        self.is_paused.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
        let _ = self.state_tx.send(PlaybackState::Stopped);
        let _ = self.cmd_tx.send(TtsCommand::Stop);
    }

    /// Toggle pause / resume
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub fn toggle_pause(&self) {
        let _ = self.cmd_tx.send(TtsCommand::TogglePause);
    }

    /// Change active voice (e.g. "af_heart", "bf_isabella", "am_puck", "bm_fable")
    pub fn set_voice(&self, voice: &str) {
        if let Ok(mut guard) = self.voice.lock() {
            *guard = voice.to_string();
        }
    }

    /// Change speech speed (0.6x to 2.5x)
    pub fn set_speed(&self, speed: f32) {
        self.speed_bits.store(speed.to_bits(), Ordering::SeqCst);
    }

    /// Change volume (0.0 to 1.0)
    pub fn set_volume(&self, volume: f32) {
        let clamped = volume.clamp(0.0, 2.0);
        self.volume_bits.store(clamped.to_bits(), Ordering::SeqCst);
        if let Ok(guard) = self.active_sink.lock() {
            if let Some(ref s) = *guard {
                s.set_volume(clamped);
            }
        }
    }
}



===== FILE: E:\Speak-That-Windows\src\bionic\engine.rs =====
/// Native Bionic Reading Engine for Windows
/// Supports:
/// - Parsing text into structured bionic tokens (for native GUI renderers)
/// - Converting text to Mathematical Bold Unicode glyphs for universal in-place injection across any app
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct BionicWord {
    pub bold: String,
    pub rest: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BionicToken {
    Word(BionicWord),
    NonWord(String),
}

pub struct BionicEngine {
    pub fixation_ratio: f32,
}

impl Default for BionicEngine {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            fixation_ratio: 0.4,
        }
    }
}

impl BionicEngine {
    pub fn new(fixation_ratio: f32) -> Self {
        Self {
            fixation_ratio: fixation_ratio.clamp(0.1, 0.9),
        }
    }

    /// Calculate the number of characters to bold at the start of a word
    pub fn get_bold_length(len: usize, ratio: f32) -> usize {
        if len <= 1 {
            1
        } else if len <= 3 {
            len.min((len as f32 * ratio).ceil() as usize).max(1)
        } else if len == 4 {
            3.min((len as f32 * ratio).ceil() as usize).max(1)
        } else {
            (len - 1).min((len as f32 * ratio).ceil() as usize).max(1)
        }
    }

    /// Map standard Latin letters and digits to Mathematical Bold Sans-Serif Unicode glyphs
    pub fn to_bold_char(c: char) -> char {
        match c {
            'A'..='Z' => {
                let offset = (c as u32) - ('A' as u32);
                char::from_u32(0x1D5D4 + offset).unwrap_or(c)
            }
            'a'..='z' => {
                let offset = (c as u32) - ('a' as u32);
                char::from_u32(0x1D5EE + offset).unwrap_or(c)
            }
            '0'..='9' => {
                let offset = (c as u32) - ('0' as u32);
                char::from_u32(0x1D7EC + offset).unwrap_or(c)
            }
            _ => c,
        }
    }

    /// Parse a single word into bold and rest parts
    pub fn process_word(&self, word: &str) -> BionicWord {
        let chars: Vec<char> = word.chars().collect();
        let bold_len = Self::get_bold_length(chars.len(), self.fixation_ratio);

        let bold: String = chars[..bold_len].iter().collect();
        let rest: String = chars[bold_len..].iter().collect();

        BionicWord { bold, rest }
    }

    /// Tokenize arbitrary text into words and delimiters
    pub fn tokenize(&self, text: &str) -> Vec<BionicToken> {
        let mut tokens = Vec::new();
        let mut current_word = String::new();
        let mut current_non_word = String::new();

        for c in text.chars() {
            if c.is_alphanumeric() {
                if !current_non_word.is_empty() {
                    tokens.push(BionicToken::NonWord(std::mem::take(&mut current_non_word)));
                }
                current_word.push(c);
            } else {
                if !current_word.is_empty() {
                    let word = std::mem::take(&mut current_word);
                    tokens.push(BionicToken::Word(self.process_word(&word)));
                }
                current_non_word.push(c);
            }
        }

        if !current_word.is_empty() {
            tokens.push(BionicToken::Word(self.process_word(&current_word)));
        }
        if !current_non_word.is_empty() {
            tokens.push(BionicToken::NonWord(current_non_word));
        }

        tokens
    }

    /// Convert text into Mathematical Bold Sans-Serif Unicode format
    /// E.g. "Reading is" -> "𝗥𝗲𝗮ding 𝗶s"
    /// Can be pasted into any Windows input field directly
    pub fn to_unicode_bionic(&self, text: &str) -> String {
        let tokens = self.tokenize(text);
        let mut result = String::with_capacity(text.len() * 2);

        for token in tokens {
            match token {
                BionicToken::Word(w) => {
                    for c in w.bold.chars() {
                        result.push(Self::to_bold_char(c));
                    }
                    result.push_str(&w.rest);
                }
                BionicToken::NonWord(nw) => {
                    result.push_str(&nw);
                }
            }
        }

        result
    }
}

===== FILE: E:\Speak-That-Windows\src\clipboard\selection.rs =====
use std::time::Duration;
use tracing::info;
use windows::Win32::Foundation::{HANDLE, HGLOBAL, HWND};
use windows::Win32::System::DataExchange::{
    CloseClipboard, EmptyClipboard, GetClipboardData, GetClipboardSequenceNumber, OpenClipboard,
    SetClipboardData,
};
use windows::Win32::System::Memory::{GlobalAlloc, GlobalLock, GlobalUnlock, GHND};
use windows::Win32::UI::Input::KeyboardAndMouse::{
    MapVirtualKeyW, SendInput, INPUT, INPUT_0, INPUT_KEYBOARD, KEYBDINPUT, KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY,
    KEYEVENTF_KEYUP, MAPVK_VK_TO_VSC, VIRTUAL_KEY, VK_C, VK_CONTROL, VK_LCONTROL, VK_LMENU,
    VK_LSHIFT, VK_LWIN, VK_RCONTROL, VK_RMENU, VK_RSHIFT, VK_RWIN,
};
use windows::Win32::UI::WindowsAndMessaging::{GetForegroundWindow, GetWindowTextW};

const CF_UNICODETEXT: u32 = 13;

pub struct SelectionCapture;

impl SelectionCapture {
    fn foreground_window_title() -> String {
        unsafe {
            let hwnd = GetForegroundWindow();
            if hwnd.0.is_null() {
                return String::from("<none>");
            }
            let mut buf = [0u16; 256];
            let len = GetWindowTextW(hwnd, &mut buf);
            if len <= 0 {
                return String::from("<untitled>");
            }
            String::from_utf16_lossy(&buf[..len as usize])
        }
    }

    fn key_input(vk: VIRTUAL_KEY, up: bool, extended: bool) -> INPUT {
        let scan = unsafe { MapVirtualKeyW(vk.0 as u32, MAPVK_VK_TO_VSC) as u16 };
        let mut flags = Default::default();
        if up {
            flags |= KEYEVENTF_KEYUP;
        }
        if extended {
            flags |= KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY;
        }
        INPUT {
            r#type: INPUT_KEYBOARD,
            Anonymous: INPUT_0 {
                ki: KEYBDINPUT {
                    wVk: vk,
                    wScan: scan,
                    dwFlags: flags,
                    time: 0,
                    dwExtraInfo: 0,
                },
            },
        }
    }

    /// Read Unicode text currently stored in the Windows clipboard
    pub fn read_clipboard_text() -> Option<String> {
        unsafe {
            if OpenClipboard(HWND(std::ptr::null_mut())).is_err() {
                return None;
            }

            let handle = match GetClipboardData(CF_UNICODETEXT) {
                Ok(h) => h,
                Err(_) => {
                    let _ = CloseClipboard();
                    return None;
                }
            };

            if handle.is_invalid() {
                let _ = CloseClipboard();
                return None;
            }

            let ptr = GlobalLock(HGLOBAL(handle.0)) as *const u16;
            if ptr.is_null() {
                let _ = CloseClipboard();
                return None;
            }

            let mut len = 0;
            while *ptr.add(len) != 0 {
                len += 1;
            }

            let slice = std::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr, len);
            let text = String::from_utf16_lossy(slice);

            let _ = GlobalUnlock(HGLOBAL(handle.0));
            let _ = CloseClipboard();

            Some(text)
        }
    }

    /// Write Unicode text directly to the Windows clipboard
    pub fn write_clipboard_text(text: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
        let utf16: Vec<u16> = text.encode_utf16().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect();
        let bytes_len = utf16.len() * std::mem::size_of::<u16>();

        unsafe {
            let h_mem =
                GlobalAlloc(GHND, bytes_len).map_err(|e| format!("GlobalAlloc failed: {e:?}"))?;
            let ptr = GlobalLock(h_mem) as *mut u16;
            if ptr.is_null() {
                return Err("GlobalLock failed".to_string());
            }

            std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(utf16.as_ptr(), ptr, utf16.len());
            let _ = GlobalUnlock(h_mem);

            OpenClipboard(HWND(std::ptr::null_mut()))
                .map_err(|e| format!("OpenClipboard failed: {e:?}"))?;
            let _ = EmptyClipboard();
            let _ = SetClipboardData(CF_UNICODETEXT, HANDLE(h_mem.0));
            let _ = CloseClipboard();
        }

        Ok(())
    }

    /// Releases any held modifier keys, sends a clean synthetic Ctrl+C, and polls
    /// `GetClipboardSequenceNumber()` before reading the newly copied selection.
    pub async fn capture_selected_text_synthetic(timeout: Duration) -> Result<String, String> {
        let fg_title = Self::foreground_window_title();
        let backup = Self::read_clipboard_text();

        // Clear clipboard temporarily so stale data cannot bleed through
        unsafe {
            if OpenClipboard(HWND(std::ptr::null_mut())).is_ok() {
                let _ = EmptyClipboard();
                let _ = CloseClipboard();
            }
        }

        // 1. Explicitly release all held modifier keys so the target app sees a clean Ctrl+C
        let release_mods = [
            Self::key_input(VK_LWIN, true, true),
            Self::key_input(VK_RWIN, true, true),
            Self::key_input(VK_LMENU, true, false),
            Self::key_input(VK_RMENU, true, true),
            Self::key_input(VK_LSHIFT, true, false),
            Self::key_input(VK_RSHIFT, true, false),
            Self::key_input(VK_LCONTROL, true, false),
            Self::key_input(VK_RCONTROL, true, true),
        ];
        unsafe {
            SendInput(&release_mods, std::mem::size_of::<INPUT>() as i32);
        }

        // Brief settle delay so Windows / foreground app processes modifier releases
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(25)).await;

        let seq_before = unsafe { GetClipboardSequenceNumber() };

        // 2. Send clean Ctrl + C with hardware scan codes
        let copy_inputs = [
            Self::key_input(VK_CONTROL, false, false),
            Self::key_input(VK_C, false, false),
            Self::key_input(VK_C, true, false),
            Self::key_input(VK_CONTROL, true, false),
        ];
        let sent_count = unsafe { SendInput(&copy_inputs, std::mem::size_of::<INPUT>() as i32) };

        // 3. Poll every 15ms up to max(timeout, 300ms) until clipboard sequence increments
        let max_wait = timeout.max(Duration::from_millis(300));
        let start = std::time::Instant::now();
        let mut captured: Option<String> = None;
        let mut seq_after = seq_before;

        while start.elapsed() < max_wait {
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(15)).await;
            let seq_now = unsafe { GetClipboardSequenceNumber() };
            if seq_now != seq_before {
                seq_after = seq_now;
                if let Some(text) = Self::read_clipboard_text() {
                    if !text.trim().is_empty() {
                        captured = Some(text);
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        info!(
            "SelectionCapture fg=\"{}\" send_input={}/{} seq={}->{} captured_chars={}",
            fg_title,
            sent_count,
            copy_inputs.len(),
            seq_before,
            seq_after,
            captured.as_ref().map(|s| s.len()).unwrap_or(0)
        );

        let result = captured.ok_or_else(|| "No text selected in active window".to_string());

        // Restore previous clipboard text if present
        if let Some(old) = backup {
            let _ = Self::write_clipboard_text(&old);
        }

        result
    }
}



===== FILE: E:\Speak-That-Windows\src\downloader\mod.rs =====
use futures_util::StreamExt;
use reqwest::Client;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
use std::fs::OpenOptions;
use std::io::Write;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Instant;
use tokio::sync::watch;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]
pub enum DownloadState {
    NotInstalled,
    Downloading {
        progress: f32, // 0.0 to 1.0
        bytes_downloaded: u64,
        total_bytes: u64,
        speed_bps: u64,
    },
    Paused {
        bytes_downloaded: u64,
        total_bytes: u64,
    },
    VerifyingHash,
    Installed,
    Error(String),
}

pub struct ModelDownloader {
    client: Client,
    state_tx: watch::Sender<DownloadState>,
}

impl ModelDownloader {
    pub const PARAKEET_URL: &'static str =
        "https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3/resolve/main/model.int8.onnx";
    pub const EXPECTED_SHA256: &'static str =
        "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"; // Checksum anchor

    pub fn new() -> (Self, watch::Receiver<DownloadState>) {
        let (state_tx, state_rx) = watch::channel(DownloadState::NotInstalled);
        (
            Self {
                client: Client::builder().build().unwrap_or_default(),
                state_tx,
            },
            state_rx,
        )
    }

    pub fn model_dir() -> PathBuf {
        let base = dirs::data_local_dir().unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("."));
        base.join("SpeakThat").join("models")
    }

    pub fn model_file_path() -> PathBuf {
        Self::model_dir().join("parakeet-tdt-0.6b.onnx")
    }

    pub fn is_model_installed() -> bool {
        let p = Self::model_file_path();
        p.exists() && p.metadata().map(|m| m.len() > 1_000_000).unwrap_or(false)
    }

    pub async fn start_download(self: Arc<Self>) -> Result<(), String> {
        let dir = Self::model_dir();
        tokio::fs::create_dir_all(&dir)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to create models directory: {}", e))?;

        let final_path = Self::model_file_path();
        let part_path = dir.join("parakeet-tdt-0.6b.part");

        let existing_bytes = if part_path.exists() {
            tokio::fs::metadata(&part_path).await.map(|m| m.len()).unwrap_or(0)
        } else {
            0
        };

        let mut req = self.client.get(Self::PARAKEET_URL);
        if existing_bytes > 0 {
            req = req.header("Range", format!("bytes={}-", existing_bytes));
        }

        let res = req
            .send()
            .await
            .map_err(|e| format!("Network connection failed: {}", e))?;

        let total_bytes = res
            .content_length()
            .map(|l| l + existing_bytes)
            .unwrap_or(600_000_000); // ~600 MB default estimated size

        let mut file = OpenOptions::new()
            .create(true)
            .append(true)
            .open(&part_path)
            .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to open part file: {}", e))?;

        let mut downloaded = existing_bytes;
        let mut last_instant = Instant::now();
        let mut last_downloaded = downloaded;
        let mut stream = res.bytes_stream();

        while let Some(chunk) = stream.next().await {
            let chunk = chunk.map_err(|e| format!("Download stream interrupted: {}", e))?;
            file.write_all(&chunk)
                .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to write chunk to disk: {}", e))?;
            downloaded += chunk.len() as u64;

            let elapsed = last_instant.elapsed();
            if elapsed.as_millis() >= 250 {
                let speed_bps = if elapsed.as_secs_f32() > 0.0 {
                    ((downloaded - last_downloaded) as f32 / elapsed.as_secs_f32()) as u64
                } else {
                    0
                };
                last_instant = Instant::now();
                last_downloaded = downloaded;

                let progress = if total_bytes > 0 {
                    (downloaded as f32 / total_bytes as f32).min(1.0)
                } else {
                    0.0
                };

                let _ = self.state_tx.send(DownloadState::Downloading {
                    progress,
                    bytes_downloaded: downloaded,
                    total_bytes,
                    speed_bps,
                });
            }
        }

        // Verify Hash
        let _ = self.state_tx.send(DownloadState::VerifyingHash);
        let bytes = tokio::fs::read(&part_path)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to read part for hash verification: {}", e))?;
        let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
        hasher.update(&bytes);
        let calculated = format!("{:x}", hasher.finalize());
        if !Self::EXPECTED_SHA256.is_empty() && calculated != Self::EXPECTED_SHA256 {
            tracing::warn!("Model hash mismatch! Calculated: {}, Expected: {}", calculated, Self::EXPECTED_SHA256);
        }

        tokio::fs::rename(part_path, final_path)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to finalize model file: {}", e))?;

        let _ = self.state_tx.send(DownloadState::Installed);
        Ok(())
    }
}



===== FILE: E:\Speak-That-Windows\src\input\catalog.rs =====
use super::chord::{InputChord, ModifierKey, TriggerSource};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CollisionSeverity {
    Allowed,
    Warning(String),
    HardBlocked(String),
}

pub struct ShortcutCatalog;

impl ShortcutCatalog {
    /// Validates an input chord against Windows OS and application shortcuts.
    ///
    /// Rules:
    /// - Keyboard combinations of 2 to 4 keys are permitted (1-key allowed when `allow_single_key` is true, or for F1-F12 / Mouse).
    /// - Critical OS operations (Lock, Task Manager, Clipboard, Close) use exact modifier-set matching and are hard-blocked.
    /// - Common editor/browser shortcuts (Ctrl+S, Ctrl+F, etc.) use exact modifier-set matching and produce soft warnings.
    pub fn validate(chord: &InputChord) -> CollisionSeverity {
        Self::validate_for(chord, false)
    }

    pub fn validate_for(chord: &InputChord, allow_single_key: bool) -> CollisionSeverity {
        let total_keys = chord.total_keys_count();

        // Validate key length range: max 4 keys
        if total_keys > 4 {
            return CollisionSeverity::HardBlocked(
                "Shortcuts cannot exceed 4 keys (e.g. Ctrl + Shift + Alt + Key).".into(),
            );
        }

        let has_ctrl = chord.modifiers.contains(&ModifierKey::Control);
        let has_alt = chord.modifiers.contains(&ModifierKey::Alt);
        let has_shift = chord.modifiers.contains(&ModifierKey::Shift);
        let has_win = chord.modifiers.contains(&ModifierKey::Win);

        let exact_mods = |ctrl: bool, shift: bool, alt: bool, win: bool| -> bool {
            has_ctrl == ctrl && has_shift == shift && has_alt == alt && has_win == win
        };

        if let TriggerSource::Key(vk) = chord.trigger {
            // Single key rule: F1-F12 always allowed; single keys allowed for Home Dashboard when opted in
            if chord.modifiers.is_empty() && !(0x70..=0x7B).contains(&vk) && !allow_single_key {
                return CollisionSeverity::HardBlocked(
                    "Requires 2-4 keys (add Ctrl, Alt, Win, or Shift), or use F1-F12.".into(),
                );
            }

            // --- HARD BLOCKS (Exact modifier-set matching for Windows OS Critical) ---
            if exact_mods(false, false, false, true) && vk == 0x20 {
                return CollisionSeverity::HardBlocked(
                    "Win + Space is reserved by Windows (Keyboard Layout Switcher).".into(),
                );
            }
            if exact_mods(false, false, false, true) && vk == 0x4C {
                return CollisionSeverity::HardBlocked("Win + L is reserved by Windows (Lock).".into());
            }
            if exact_mods(false, false, true, false) && vk == 0x73 {
                return CollisionSeverity::HardBlocked("Alt + F4 is reserved by Windows (Close Window).".into());
            }
            if exact_mods(true, false, true, false) && vk == 0x2E {
                return CollisionSeverity::HardBlocked("Ctrl + Alt + Delete is reserved by Windows Security.".into());
            }
            if exact_mods(false, false, false, true) && vk == 0x44 {
                return CollisionSeverity::HardBlocked("Win + D is reserved by Windows (Show Desktop).".into());
            }
            if exact_mods(true, true, false, false) && vk == 0x1B {
                return CollisionSeverity::HardBlocked("Ctrl + Shift + Esc is reserved for Task Manager.".into());
            }
            if exact_mods(false, false, true, false) && vk == 0x09 {
                return CollisionSeverity::HardBlocked("Alt + Tab is reserved for window switching.".into());
            }

            // Universal Edit Operations (strictly Ctrl+<Key>, NOT Ctrl+Shift+<Key>)
            if exact_mods(true, false, false, false) {
                match vk {
                    0x43 => return CollisionSeverity::HardBlocked("Ctrl + C is reserved for Copy.".into()),
                    0x56 => return CollisionSeverity::HardBlocked("Ctrl + V is reserved for Paste.".into()),
                    0x58 => return CollisionSeverity::HardBlocked("Ctrl + X is reserved for Cut.".into()),
                    0x5A => return CollisionSeverity::HardBlocked("Ctrl + Z is reserved for Undo.".into()),
                    0x41 => return CollisionSeverity::HardBlocked("Ctrl + A is reserved for Select All.".into()),
                    // --- SOFT WARNINGS (Exact modifier-set matching) ---
                    0x53 => {
                        return CollisionSeverity::Warning(
                            "Ctrl + S is commonly used for Save in editors and Office apps.".into(),
                        );
                    }
                    0x46 => {
                        return CollisionSeverity::Warning(
                            "Ctrl + F is commonly used for Find in browsers and viewers.".into(),
                        );
                    }
                    0x50 => {
                        return CollisionSeverity::Warning(
                            "Ctrl + P is commonly used for Print in browsers and office apps.".into(),
                        );
                    }
                    0x54 => {
                        return CollisionSeverity::Warning(
                            "Ctrl + T is commonly used for New Tab in web browsers.".into(),
                        );
                    }
                    0x57 => {
                        return CollisionSeverity::Warning(
                            "Ctrl + W is commonly used for Close Tab in web browsers.".into(),
                        );
                    }
                    _ => {}
                }
            }
        }

        CollisionSeverity::Allowed
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {

    fn default_shortcuts_have_no_false_positive_warnings() {

            CollisionSeverity::Allowed
        );

            CollisionSeverity::Allowed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            ShortcutCatalog::validate_for(&cfg.shortcuts.push_to_talk.keyboard, false),
            CollisionSeverity::Allowed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            ShortcutCatalog::validate_for(&cfg.shortcuts.open_home.keyboard, true),
            CollisionSeverity::Allowed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            ShortcutCatalog::validate_for(&cfg.shortcuts.toggle_bionic.keyboard, false),
            CollisionSeverity::Allowed
        );
        assert_eq!(
            ShortcutCatalog::validate_for(&cfg.shortcuts.toggle_reader.keyboard, false),
            CollisionSeverity::Allowed
        );
    }
